homeAboutText.zh: 马来西亚人，毕业于马来亚大学地质系，现在在京都大学做地震研究。"金釘子"取自地质学的 Golden Spike（GSSP），也就是定义地质年代分界的标准点。
homeAboutText.en: From Malaysia, trained in geology at the University of Malaya, now doing earthquake research at Kyoto University. A Golden Spike (GSSP) is the reference point that defines a boundary in geologic time.

myLead.zh: 会，只是比较少，而且通常不大。西马的地震主要来自两个地方：苏门答腊外海的大地震，还有我们脚下的老断层。东马的沙巴离板块边界更近，地震也多得多。
myLead.en: Yes, just not often, and usually not big ones. West Malaysia feels quakes from two places: big earthquakes off Sumatra, and old faults right under our feet. Sabah, in East Malaysia, is closer to plate boundaries and gets a lot more.

myHistNote.zh: 地图上的点来自 USGS，网站每小时更新一次。西马本地的地震多半太小，USGS 没有收录，最完整的纪录要看大马气象局（MetMalaysia）。觉得有地震时，也可以到 MetMalaysia 网站查最新公告。
myHistNote.en: Dots come from USGS and the site refreshes every hour. Most local quakes in the peninsula are too small for USGS to list, so MetMalaysia has the fullest record. If you think you felt one, MetMalaysia is also where the latest announcements go up.

gsLead.zh: 地质年代表上的每一条分界，都钉在地球某处真实的岩层上。这里是目前所有已经批准的金钉子，点一下就能看到它在哪里、靠什么认出来。
gsLead.en: Every boundary on the geologic time scale is pinned to a real layer of rock somewhere on Earth. These are all the golden spikes ratified so far. Tap one to see where it is and how geologists recognise it.

gsPick.zh: 点地图上的金色圆点，或在下面的时间轴选一个纪，就能看到那根金钉子的资料。
gsPick.en: Tap a gold dot on the map, or pick a period on the timeline below, to see that golden spike.

gsSource.zh: 资料：International Commission on Stratigraphy（ICS）GSSP 表，2026 年 11 月整理；颜色是国际年代地层表的官方配色。
gsSource.en: Data: International Commission on Stratigraphy (ICS) GSSP table, compiled November 2026. Colours follow the official International Chronostratigraphic Chart.
